title: Staged Promotion Policy Engine for Hosted/Dedicated/Private with Shadowing & Auto-Revert
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Build a single policy-driven 'staged promotion' engine that standardizes progressive promotion workflows (canary-style traffic ramp, A/B percentile experiments, shadow/mirroring) across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments while respecting environment constraints (network egress, KMS/HSM access, RBAC, capacity limits).

Why: Current ad-hoc scripts and controller variants create maintenance burden and inconsistent behavior when teams try to promote a model from hosted to dedicated or to a customer's private cluster. We need a predictable promotion surface that: 1) allows teams to declare safety gates and rollback conditions, 2) performs environment-aware checks before each promotion step, and 3) supports shadow traffic and A/B experiments without violating data residency or security policies in Private mode.

Scope: policy DSL, control-plane APIs, runtime adapters for routing (hosted router, dedicated traffic manager, private agent), auto-rollback heuristics, observability hooks (per-step metrics and traces), e2e test harness. Not in scope: training lifecycle or model artifact signing (handled by upstream).
acceptance_criteria: Policy DSL: teams can declare staged promotion flows (sequence of steps with traffic %s, duration, thresholds, and fallback targets) using a JSON/YAML policy and apply to any environment.
Environment checks: before executing a step the engine validates environment constraints (network egress, KMS availability, quota) and surfaces human-readable failures.
Shadowing: engine supports safe shadowing with configurable sampling and strict PII/data-routing policies for Private deployments (no outbound telemetry to hosted control plane unless consented).
Auto-revert: rollback triggers (error rate, latency regression, embed quality drift) are configurable per-policy and will execute automated revert within defined cooldown windows.
Parity: same high-level policy semantics work across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private; environment-specific adapters implement the differences behind a uniform API.
Observability: each promotion step emits standard metrics (traffic %, errors, p50/p95 latency, token cost delta) and a dashboard template exists for SRE/PM review.
Integration tests: CI harness exercises at least three flows: basic canary ramp, parallel A/B test, and shadow-only traffic with simulated private constraints.
implementation_steps: Design policy DSL and API contract (3 days): define fields for steps, thresholds, mirroring, and fallback targets.
Implement controller core (6 days): state machine, step scheduler, policy parsing, plugin model for environment adapters.
Build adapters (hosted, dedicated manager, private agent) (10 days): routing calls to existing routers, applying environment-specific pre-checks.
Auto-rollback engine (4 days): threshold evaluation, cooldown, safe revert orchestration, rollback runbook hooks.
Observability (3 days): metrics schema, trace spans, and dashboard template; hook into Console's rollout timeline.
E2E tests and canary CI (5 days): simulator for traffic, failure injection, and private-env constraints.
Docs and runbook (2 days): operator guide, policy examples, and customer migration notes.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Automated rollback may oscillate under noisy signals. Mitigation: require multi-metric confirmation and configurable cooldown windows before revert.

Risk: Private deployments cannot reach hosted control plane for policy coordination. Mitigation: support a local agent that enforces policies with offline sync and clear audit logs; default to manual step if critical checks fail.
Risk: Shadowing may leak PII or violate contracts. Mitigation: add strict policy flags that block payload forwarding in Private mode and require explicit customer consent for any external telemetry.
Risk: Capacity mismatch in Dedicated during ramp. Mitigation: pre-step quota checks and automatic throttling with backpressure signals to clients.
